_comment: Best measured mean q_score per task, and the run that produced it. scripts/read_run.py compares a run
against this, so a regression is caught by reading the run rather than by remembering. Update an entry only
when a run beats it on the SAME instances -- a different instance set is a different measurement. Every
number here was taken with --knowledge oracle and sticky grasping, which the challenge does not allow; they
measure the planning and motion pipeline, not a submission.
instance_count is what read_run.py compares: a run over a different number of instances is not a like-for-like comparison, however its mean turns out.

Two runs of the same code on the same two instances of putting_away_toys gave blocked-motion counts of 46 and 62 and empty-mask counts of 9 and 17. Treat a single run's counts as an observation, not a measurement.
dispose_of_batteries is worse: the same code over the same two instances gave means of 0.375 and 0.125. Before crediting or blaming a change on either task, repeat the run.

turning_on_radio.note: STALE, do not compare against it: pass 6 ran on 2026-09-10 06:59 and the capture speed cap (CAPTURE_MAX_JOINT_VEL, commit 6cf430432) landed 2026-09-11 00:27, so this number was measured with observation swings that slammed the arms at the joints' full speed. Re-measure before using it.

assembling_gift_baskets.note: single instance best: 0.875 on 301 in the 2026-09-12 regression Check the date against commit 6cf430432 (the capture speed cap, 2026-09-11 00:27) before comparing: a pass that predates it was measured with uncapped observation swings.

dispose_of_batteries.note: Ten instances, one solved completely (304). Per instance: 0.25, 0.50, 0.50, 1.00, 0.50, 0.25, 0.00, 0.25, 0.00, 0.50. This is the first number for this task worth comparing against -- two instances gave 0.375 and 0.125 on identical code. The composition has shifted: 30 rounds executed, 30 lost to PLANNING and 14 to empty masks, all 54 cuTAMP failures being 'motion planning failed for N/N satisfying particles'. battery_3 is unplaced in 8 of the 10.

putting_away_toys.note: 0.75 and 0.875, seven of eight toys placed in one instance, and runs/bench_toys_8 repeated it exactly. Two runs before the ramp block-test and presenting fixes gave 0.4375 and 0.375. Read scores, not mechanism counts: runs 7 and 8 are the same behaviour for this task and gave 9 against 17 rounds lost to empty masks and 46 against 62 blocked arm motions, which is this task's noise floor.

picking_up_trash.note: Solved completely on the task's first ever run, 5 rounds, 1055 s. Three cans of soda off one floor into a trash can on another; the cans are 7-8.3 cm across against a jaw that opens to 8 cm, which was the reason for trying it. One instance only.

re_shelving_library_books.note: First run: 0.0, with 10 planning failures and 8 rounds lost to empty masks, one round executed and an item released. A bookcase is an opening entered from the SIDE, unlike every container the pipeline has placed into, and the shelf above the target slot is in the way of a top-down approach.

store_honey.note: First run: 0.0, but the pick and the place both executed -- the jar finished ON the cabinet (bottom z 0.84, cabinet top 0.85). Nothing is wrong with the transfer; the cabinet has to be opened first. The cheapest end-to-end test of an open/close skill in the challenge set.
